submission.natural_language_explanation: It fires on a hiragana token that continues a hiragana run (the token immediately to its left is also hiragana) - the grammatical, kanji-free stretches of Japanese - and, much more rarely but just as strongly, on the second token of a memorised Latin-script bigram ('of course', 'Here is', 'very much', 'among other', 'a lot of', 'General Public License', 'Hold on', 'Check out') or on the continuation fragment of a token-split word (O|gn|jen, R|is|eman, t|ak|ze). The same token in a different left context stays near zero ('of course' 2.9 vs 'a course' 0.0, 'Here is' 1.3 vs 'There is' 0.0, 'Ognjen' 2.5 vs 'Vognjen' 0.0) and the same Japanese sentence in katakana is silent (1.69 vs 0.0), so the pole is a conjunction of the current token with its immediate left neighbour, not a token-identity or surprisal detector.
